title: Congestion mitigator and soft-reserve patterns — PRD draft
content:
Context / TL;DR:

We keep hearing two recurring customer asks for Dedicated: (1) predictable latency under sudden spikes without over-reserving (cost pressure), and (2) strong tenant isolation when noisy neighbors emerge. This PRD proposes a combined "congestion mitigator" runtime component + a soft-reserve pattern (policy construct in control plane) that together provide low-latency headroom for short bursts while preserving isolation guarantees and predictable economics.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce P99 latency spikes for tenants experiencing short traffic surges by 40–60% versus current baseline without increasing committed GPU reservations by >10% on average.
- Provide operational controls for platform teams to set per-tenant degradation envelopes (isolation fences) that are honored during overloads.
- Enable chargeback and billing signals so customers can opt into paid transient headroom (burst) or automatic graceful degradation.
- Expose observability surfaces in Console: per-tenant congestion events, preemption traces, burst usage metrics, and cost impact.

Non-goals:
- This is not a wholesale replacement for long-lived reservations or committed capacity contracts.
- We are not building a marketplace for cross-tenant borrowing of capacity in this phase.

User personas and example stories:
- Platform/Infra engineer (on Redwood side): wants an operator-visible way to limit the blast radius of noisy jobs, and to debug why eviction/fallback happened.
- Tenant admin (customer): wants their low-latency product routes to stay healthy during sudden traffic spikes but only pay for transient headroom when used.
- Solutions engineer: wants to explain tradeoffs and help customers tune soft-reserve and fallback policies.

Primary concepts (terminology):
- Soft-reserve: a configurable credit balance that a tenant can borrow from for a short time window. It is not a hard reservation; it can be revoked or gracefully decayed when platform-level constraints require it.
- Congestion mitigator: runtime shim between router and scheduler that detects short-term token-level demand bursts and routes matching requests to prewarmed micro-pools, or applies controlled graceful degradation (quantization switch, lower sampling, model variant fallback).
- Isolation fence: per-tenant policy including latency SLOs, eviction priority, minimum guaranteed concurrency, and max-burst budget.

High-level design:
1) Control plane: add a soft-reserve object tied to tenant account. Fields: burst_budget_tokens, refill_rate, max_burst_duration, billing_mode (free-with-capacity, prepaid-credits, pay-as-used), isolation_class (strict, standard, lenient), fallback_policy_id.
2) Runtime shim (congestion mitigator): lightweight traffic analyser per-route that looks at moving-window QPS, token consumption rate, and KV cache hit ratios. If burst is detected and tenant has available soft-reserve credits, the shim routes to either: (a) prewarmed micro-pool (fast path) if slots available; (b) compatible lower-cost quantized model variant; or (c) triggers batching tweaks (increase batch size for opportunistic throughput) if latency envelope allows. If no credits, it enforces isolation fence via queueing or rejecting excess requests to fallback lane.
3) Admission stitching and metrics: every decision emits events: CREDIT_CONSUMED, PREWARM_ALLOC, FALLBACK_TRIGGER, ISOLATION_ENFORCED. Console surfaces for humans and SLI pipelines will consume these.

Behavioral details / heuristics:
- Burst detection window: default 15s sliding window with tunable sensitivity per-tenant. A spike is defined as >3x median QPS for the window or a sudden token-rate increase above 95th percentile.
- Prewarm micro-pools: small pools reserved for low-latency spikes (e.g., 1–4 GPU-backed workers, ephemeral). These are cold-start optimized (prefetch KV cache, keep small model shard warmed). Prewarms should be recycled aggressively to avoid cost accumulation.
- Credit accounting: credits charged proportional to token-usage * model-weight factor. Refill: slow trickle (e.g., 1 credit / min) or purchased top-ups.
- Graceful degrade sequence (ordered): try model-variant fallback -> enable transient batching -> reduce response fidelity (sampling/streaming chunk) -> last resort: 429 / reject with guidance.

API and operator UX:
- Console: SoftReserve panel in tenant settings. Simple slider for max-burst-duration and billing mode, plus fine-grain "isolation fence" builder.
- CLI/Infra API: POST /tenants/{id}/soft_reserve {budget, refill_rate, billing_mode}, GET /tenants/{id}/congestion_events?since=...
- Alerts: Built-in alerts for when soft-reserve consumption > 70% for 5m, when isolation fence triggered > N times.

Observability and SLIs:
- SLIs: tenant_p99_latency, tenant_error_rate, prewarm_hit_rate, credits_consumed_per_min, fallback_rate.
- Logs/Traces: every decision should propagate request tags so traces show prewarm or fallback steps.
- Cost telemetry: attribute GPU-seconds from prewarm micro-pools to tenant credits or platform pool.

Telemetry and chargeback model:
- Two billing modes: auto-pay-per-use (platform bills token-weighted price at end of billing cycle) or prepaid credits (tenant uploads credits, consumed first).
- Default small free buffer for new tenants (onboarding credits) to avoid immediate throttling; indicate in Console and UX.

Operational runbook (initial):
- When platform-wide GPU utilization > 85% for > 10m, auto-disable new prewarms (global kill-switch) and increase sensitivity of isolation fences.
- If a tenant consistently uses > X% of prewarm for > 30m, recommend moving to Dedicated Reserved capacity.
- Escalation: if noisy tenant triggers > 3 isolation events in 1 hour, automated soft-quarantine (reduce burst budget by 50%) + pager for infra lead.

Implementation phasing (MVP -> v1 -> v2):
- MVP (Q1): control plane soft-reserve object, basic credit accounting, conservative runtime shim that chooses between prewarm (if available) and fallback 429. Minimal Console UI.
- v1 (Q2): integrate prewarmed micro-pools, model-variant fallbacks, observability hooks. Billing pipeline for pay-per-use credits. Operator tooling to manually adjust fences.
- v2 (future): ML-driven burst predictor to prewarm before burst (predictive warm), cross-tenant ephemeral borrowing marketplace (experimental), per-route micro-SLOs.

Risks and open questions:
- Cost leak risk: prewarms left running due to buggy lifecycle -> need hard TTL and billing guardrails.
- Complexity in tenant billing disputes: need clear audit trail of credit consumption events.
- Interaction with Dedicated autoscaler: when autoscaler starts scaling up nodes, how do prewarms interact? Avoid double-paying for warm-up.
- Open: exact credit pricing model (token-weight mult for different model families).

Metrics to evaluate success (first 90 days after launch):
- P99 reduction for bursty tenants (target 40–60%).
- Prewarm cost as % of tenant revenue (target < 3% for non-paying tenants).
- Number of customers adopting soft-reserve vs long-term reservations.
- Reduction in escalations related to noisy neighbors.

Notes to self / TODOs (brainstorm, rough):
- Simulate traffic patterns (cold starts + microbursts) in ops sim harness; use results to calibrate default refill_rate. (Diego take)
notes_short: draft PRD for runtime congestion mitigator + soft-reserve policy. Focus: short-burst latency, tenant isolation, operator controls. Sim required.
